attacks.claim: The go.mod adds `replace go.uber.org/zap => ../zap`, which points outside the repo at a local directory. A clean CI checkout has no ../zap, so the build fails or, where a sibling exists, unreviewed local code is compiled into the static binary distributed to on-call laptops. The pinned pseudo-version and its go.sum verification are bypassed.

printPlan diverges from computeBatches. It iterates over all hosts, so with --canary the canary appears in batch 0 and again in a later batch. It also sizes batches with int(len(hosts)*MaxSurge) instead of ceil(len(rest)*MaxSurge), so the printed batch membership and counts can differ from the real rollout. The plan on-call uses to verify a run is therefore wrong.
attacks.evidence: per := int(float64(len(hosts)) * o.MaxSurge) ... for i := 0; i < len(hosts); i += per {  vs.  size := int(math.Ceil(float64(len(rest)) * o.MaxSurge))

attacks.claim: printPlan re-implements the batching algorithm instead of calling computeBatches. The two copies already diverge, as the canary bug shows, and future batching changes will silently desynchronize the dry-run from the real rollout.
attacks.evidence: func printPlan(w io.Writer, hosts []string, o Options) { ... per := int(float64(len(hosts)) * o.MaxSurge) ... }

attacks.claim: The go.mod change contradicts its stated purpose. The replace directive overrides the zap pseudo-version bump, so the upstreamed JSON encoder fix does not reach the built binary. No go.sum entries are added for the pseudo-version.
attacks.evidence: bumps zap to pick up the JSON encoder fix we upstreamed. ... +replace go.uber.org/zap => ../zap
